pages.title: About
pages.content:
About Meguri Waste

Meguri Waste began in 2011 with a single truck at Port Alder harbour. Today seven of us run fixed weekly collections from Unit 4, Quay Road Yard, under licence WC-2011-0418.

pages.title: Streams
pages.content:
Streams

General waste, mixed recycling, glass, food and organics, and confidential paper: five streams, each with its own day tag and bin.

pages.title: A collection day
pages.content:
A collection day

From the 05:30 text notice to the 09:00 weighbridge report, every lift follows the same sequence.

pages.title: Weekly cover
pages.content:
Weekly cover

Starter €48/week, Core €96/week and Full week €158/week, plus add-ons. Prices exclude VAT; terms roll monthly with 30 days’ notice.

pages.title: Sites
pages.content:
Sites

Case notes from the offices, food halls and clinics we collect from across Port Alder.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

We use your details only to plan and run your collections and to send the reports you ask for. We do not sell them.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Terms

Weekly cover runs on monthly rolling terms with 30 days’ notice. Prices exclude VAT. Missed lifts are re-collected the same or next working day.

pages.title: Thanks
pages.content:
Thanks

Thank you. The customer desk will reply on the next working day.

posts.title: Alder Quay office tower
posts.excerpt: A 14-floor office tower moved to four sorted streams with Tuesday and Thursday lifts, leaving the dock clear before tenants arrive.
posts.content:
The Alder Quay tower has fourteen floors and one loading dock, and until last year every tenant’s waste left through it in whichever bins happened to be free. Mara Okafor walked the building with the facilities manager and counted the bin rooms, the lift times and the dock slots.

We moved the building to four sorted streams: general waste, mixed recycling, glass and food. Lifts now run on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, after the 05:30 text notice, so the dock is clear before the first tenant arrives.

Priya Nair’s weighbridge report reaches the facilities desk by 09:00 on each collection day, so the manager can see what left the building and from which stream.

posts.title: Linden Street food hall
posts.excerpt: Twenty-two stalls served by one organics lift at 06:10 every morning, clearing heavy food waste before kitchen prep begins.
posts.content:
Linden Street food hall has twenty-two stalls, and all of them cook before the doors open. Food waste is the first thing that builds up at the back door, so the food lift comes at 06:10, every day.

Tomás Ferreira’s north round brings sealed caddies out to the truck, lifts them and returns each one to its bay. Amina Yusuf visits the hall to show new stall staff what goes in the caddy and what stays out.

The hall keeps general waste and mixed recycling on the Monday to Friday cover, and the food add-on makes up the daily lift.

posts.title: Why your bins get a day tag
posts.excerpt: A small paper tag on every handle tells the driver, and your own staff, which day each bin is lifted.
posts.content:
Every bin we place on a site wears a paper tag with its collection day and stream. It is a small thing, but it means a new cleaner or a new driver never has to guess.

When a schedule changes, we change the tag on the same visit. The tag, the text notice and the weighbridge report all say the same day.
